subject: Error in compiling a recursive function

messages.author: 8cd9a172271b51da
messages.subject: Error in compiling a recursive function
parts:
Dear nimble users,

I am interested in writing a recursive function in nimble and compiling it. I found that it works before compiling, but I found the following error in compiling.

Error: evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion / options(expressions=)?

I have attached a simple example that produces the same error message. Could you please help me to get a solution?

Regards
Paritosh

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Error in compiling a recursive function
parts:
hi Paritosh,

Recursion should work in nimbleFunctions. In fact, it does work in nimbleFunctions with setup code. However your code does not have setup code. Our compilation system handles nimbleFunctions with and without setup code somewhat differently, so we'll have to look into why this particular case fails.

The following modification of your nimbleFunction should work if you are just writing a stand-alone nimbleFunction. However, if you need to use this nimbleFunction in a model, you'll probably run into problems. I'll file a bug report for us to look into fixing the problem affecting your original formulation.

nimble_recursive_factorial_gen <- nimbleFunction(
  setup = TRUE,
  run = function(x=double(0)){
       returnType(double(0))
       if(x==0 | x==1) {
        return(1)
       }  else {
           return(x*run(x-1))
       }
})

nimble_recursive_factorial <- nimble_recursive_factorial_gen()
nimble_recursive_factorial$run(4)
#[1] 24
cnimble_recursive_factorial <- compileNimble(nimble_recursive_factorial,
                                             showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
nimble_recursive_factorial$run(4)

-chris

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Error in compiling a recursive function
parts:
Dear Paritosh

When writing a sampler in nimble it can a good idea to base your code around an example found in the file MCMC_samplers.R.

All of the samplers in that file have setup code. So based on what Chris has said above, yes, that will be sufficient to avoid the bug that Chris identified. 

Best regards
David

messages.subject: Re: Error in compiling a recursive function
parts:
Hi Paritosh,

Yes, if the recursion is within the nimbleFunction that defines the user-defined sampler (presumably the recursive function is one of the additional methods in that nimbleFunction), I think it will work. 

-chris
